questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer: **Out of the box:** It depends on the leather. For the rustic brown, Crazy Horse or rustic black styles, he says yes: “I recommend you do this 100%” [1]. For most Blundstones, he reports that Blundstone's own FAQ says the boots are pretreated and that “we do not recommend treating them out of the box” [2]. The exception is rustic, Crazy Horse and rustic black leathers, which aren't pretreated and may be conditioned [3]. He hasn't covered out-of-box treatment for other leather boots. **How often:** His most recent view (2022) is that there's no fixed schedule. Treat them when they look or feel dry, and clean them first, since dirt wears leather down faster [4][5][6]. He admits he probably does it too little [5]. In his 2019 Blundstone review, he said that if you go “super crazy” with heavy use, you may need to wax them “every month maybe every week” [7]. He also advises conditioning any leather you haven't treated in a few months [8].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer: Yes, by his account the shrinking is what tightens them, and how hot the water and dryer are changes how much. **Hot wash and dryer (2023):** He says that if the STFs had gone in the dryer they would have been a lot smaller from the start than rinsed 501s [1]. He advises against tossing them in the dryer or rinsing them that hot if you want a good fit [2]. He doubts you would notice a difference if you wash them similarly to rinsed jeans [3]. **Soak and dry (2019):** In his soak test he believes the shrinking happens while they dry [4]. The waist was very tight at first, but after a week the waist and upper thigh had stretched enough to wear a belt [5]. He also guesses that frequent wearing would stretch them out to about the same size as the rinsed pair [7]. **Sizing (2025):** His rule is that you should usually go two sizes up with shrink-to-fits [6]. He hasn't covered how regular washing affects them over the long term.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer: Going by his sizing rule, the 501 STF would be about a **35x32**. He says Levi's recommends going two sizes up in the waist and two inches longer than you'd normally wear, and that it took him several pairs to accept that advice [1]. On his own STF pair he went up two sizes, to a 32 waist, and says that's because the jeans shrink down [2]. He also says you should usually go two sizes up on the shrink-to-fit 501 [3]. Applied to your usual 33x30, that means two sizes up in the waist (35) and two inches more in length (32). The videos don't cover how the 501 STF compares with the 502s, so treat this as his rule applied to your size rather than a direct size match.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer: He cuffs mainly for fit and look. Length is what matters most to him, and cuffing is how he handles jeans that run long or that he feels look better with a break. On his Levi's 501s, he cuffed them even though he would have picked a 32 length over the 30 he bought, because he feels his style suits cuffed, wider-legged pants better than uncuffed ones [1]. In his 501 STF video he says length is his first check, since jeans that look too long look bad, and the cuff shouldn't be too thick [2]. His habit has shifted on boots: he used to cuff his jeans, but now he likes them pulled down over his boots more [3]. He hasn't said more about why he cuffs in general.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail's view is that Solovairs are the better-built boot for the money, while Made in England Docs mainly win on leather and the yellow stitching. His most recent Made in England Doc video compares them with the cheaper Made in Thailand pair, not with Solovairs, so the Solovair comparison below comes from his 2022 review.

**Price and value:** He says Solovairs are cheaper than Made in England Docs [1]. He also estimates that a third of the Made in England price is the Made in England part [2], and he says the cheaper, plainer Docs are fine for most buyers. His 2023 verdict on the Made in England Docs was that they're probably not worth the extra $90 over the Thailand pair [7].

**Leather and finish:** He says the Made in England Docs have the better leather, which he thinks will age fine and is on par with Solovairs [2].

**Build and repairs:** Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [3]. He says they have a shank, which makes them more comfortable over long periods [4]. The Made in England Docs have the yellow stitching, which Solovairs lack [5].

**Quality control:** He is open about his own Solovair pair, which he says has had defects: he has worn them eight times and a tab on the back ripped off and a lace snapped [6]. He thinks it was a manufacturing defect and says he has contacted Solovair about it.

**Bottom line:** He suggests that if the yellow stitching isn't important to you, you should look at Solovairs; if it is, the Made in England Docs are the higher-quality choice [5][3].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
The main difference he points to is the welt and the extras. In his 2021 video, the 1907 has a storm welt, while the 875 is Goodyear welted, which he calls durable and water resistant, with room for cork that molds to your foot over time [5][8]. He calls the storm welt invaluable [2]. The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875, but he argues it's a better deal because it includes Red Wing's leather footbed and leather laces [1][3].

He isn't sure how the storm welt works. The popular view he's seen is that it's just another piece of leather added to the welt, but he doesn't present that as settled [4].

**Later view (2022):** In his Red Wing 3335 video, he describes the 875s and 1907s as having crepe soles [6] and as more beefily constructed, so they're the ones to choose if you need a tough boot [7]. He prefers the 3335 for hiking and walking.

The Iron Snail hasn't compared the sizing or fit of the 1907 and 875 in these videos.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
Of these four, he picks Uniqlo as the best budget buy. In his newest t-shirt roundup he says the $20 Uniqlo tee is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1], and in his June 2025 value video he calls its price-to-quality ratio "insane" [2]. Earlier, in his 2024 video, he said a heavyweight Uniqlo crew neck with a bound, ribbed collar may be "the best bargain t-shirt" [3].

**Front General Store:** He treats it as a step up in quality rather than a bargain pick. It's a $40 made-in-Japan tee with "great proportions, great feel" [4]. The open-end yarn is "a little rougher but they sanded it so it has some softness to it" [5], and he rated it 6 out of 10 for softness [11].

**Pro Club:** He liked it, saying it feels "like an old school American shirt" [6]. He called it "the roughest shirt on this list" [12] and rated it 4 out of 10 for softness [7], the lowest of the three.

**Hanes:** He calls it "your classic $10 great shirt" [9]. It's "much much softer than the Pro Club" [8], and he rated it 7 out of 10 for softness [13].

He groups Hanes with mass-market brands like Gildan [14]. In his June 2025 video he said all five shirts he had from those brands had a defect [10].

He hasn't compared these four head to head, and Pro Club isn't in his newer videos, so Uniqlo is the closest he's come to naming one best budget tee.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
Assuming "this" means the Barbour, his videos point to the Barbour as the closer fit for that mix, with a caveat about the wax. He calls its 6 oz Sylkoil fabric the lightest of the jackets in that video and says it's comfortable in spring [1][2]. He says that for the most part it isn't a designated rain jacket [3], and its storm cuffs help in bad weather [4]. In his shower test, a freshly waxed Bedale didn't leak, but he says a jacket worn for a few seasons won't be very water resistant and water will come right in [5]. His summary is that these aren't waterproof but are very water resistant when properly treated [6]. He ties added wind resistance to the thornproof finish rather than Sylkoil [7], so keeping the wax in good shape matters for both rain and wind.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
He calls it lined and comfortable, with full freedom of movement, and says it goes with anything [8][9]. He says it isn't crazy lightweight, though it's lighter than heavier waxed jackets [8]. The Iron Snail hasn't covered how the Flint and Tinder handles rain, wind or spring weather in the videos available here.

**Verdict**
For a rain, wind and spring mix, the Barbour fits his descriptions better. The Flint and Tinder suits someone who wants a lined everyday jacket and doesn't need weather performance.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer: He doesn't call a lack of lining a flaw for everyone. It's his personal preference, and he's softened on it since. In the 2023 video he called the Huckberry Waxed Trucker 'the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list' [1] and listed the missing lining as a con, because 'the one con that Rogue territory and huckberry have for me is that they are not lined' [2]. His reason is that he likes a liner so the wax doesn't touch your clothes or arms [2]. The lined jackets he discusses in his later video are different products. In his 2025 ranking he describes the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker, sold by Huckberry, as 'lined, so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin' [3]. He also says Flint and Tinder makes a wool-lined version that he hasn't tried yet [3]. That segment was a paid sponsor read from Huckberry [4]. He hasn't covered a flannel-lined Huckberry version in these videos, so I can't confirm that one. He also now says 'I kind of see why you wouldn't line something', noting that satin linings can feel sticky once it gets warm [5]. So he sees the unlined point as a matter of taste rather than a clear defect.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer: **Short answer:** The Iron Snail hasn't directly compared the fit of the Red Wing 3335s with the 875s in the videos available here. In his 2022 review of the 3335s, he says he went true to size and they fit fine [1]. They are slim, though, and taper down, so they were comfortable with thin cotton socks but his toes felt squished with wool socks, and he can't wiggle them much [2]. The closest he gets to the 875s is saying the 3335s are lighter and more nimble because of their stitchdown build, which is about how they feel to walk in rather than how they fit [3].
